routes.label: Compare the shortest side and mean
Compare three copies of the shortest side

question: The lengths of the sides of a triangle in inches are three consecutive integers. The length of the shortest side is \(30\%\) of the perimeter. What is the length of the longest side?
solution:
Compare the actual perimeter with three copies of the shortest side. Since the shortest side is \(30\%\) of the perimeter, three copies total \(3\cdot30\%=90\%\) of the perimeter.

The sides are consecutive integers, so the second side is \(1\) inch longer than the shortest and the longest is \(2\) inches longer. The actual perimeter therefore exceeds three copies of the shortest side by \(1+2=3\) inches.

Thus \(100\%-90\%=10\%\) of the perimeter is \(3\) inches. The perimeter is
\[
3\div0.10=30\text{ inches}.
\]
The shortest side is \(0.30\cdot30=9\) inches, so the sides are \(9,10,11\) inches. They form a triangle because \(9+10>11\). The longest side is \(\boxed{11}\) inches, choice E.
